rationale: Greek ὕπαρξις 'existence, subsistence, substantial reality.' Used here in cosmological apposition with ⲧϩⲩⲗⲏ 'Hyle': Matter as 'an existence' (ontological substrate).
Manichaean cosmological term for the death-zone at the cosmic midpoint, here directly identified with Hyle/Matter. Direct correspondence: the central death IS Matter.
Greek σταυρόω as Coptic verb. Used here of the cosmic crucifixion of the archontic host — bound and stretched out across the cosmic frame in the act of cosmic mingling.

Greek ἀπαρχή 'firstfruits, first portion.' Here used cosmogonically: 'the firstfruits of the Five Sons' (the captured light) and 'the firstfruits of the firmaments' (the cosmic foundation-share given to the rich son for setting up the firmaments).

Hapax in glossary. Context (archontic host, mingled, poured forth, joined to one another) requires a body-part or constitutive-element noun. Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲣⲱⲡⲉ 'limb' or related; alternatively a verbal element. Confidence low.

proposed_english: to pour forth / be poured out
rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'pour/transfer forth.' Cosmogonic verb for the archonic emission/dispersion.
Confirmation: standard Lycopolitan past speech-introducer in chapter-opening formula 'ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ ⲡϥⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ.'
Greek ἐξέδρα 'covered recess, outer hall' adapted to Coptic with directional ⲁϩⲛ- 'into.' Architectural term in the architect-house simile of the Living Spirit's cosmogonic work.

Greek ἀρετή 'virtue, excellence, capacity.' Chapter heading: ⲧⲁⲣⲉⲧⲏ ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ϩⲃⲥⲁⲩⲉ 'the Virtue of the Firmaments' — the cosmic-functional power/excellence of the firmaments as constructed by the rich son of the Living Spirit.
Lycopolitan qualitative form of ⲙⲟⲩ 'die' = Sahidic ⲙⲟⲟⲩⲧ. Modifies ⲥⲱⲙⲁ in ⲟⲩⲥⲱⲙⲁ ⲉϩⲙⲁⲩⲧ 'a dead body.'
